standard_prerequisites.name: A closed subscheme of finite presentation is cut out by a finite type quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, and the complement of the support of such an ideal is a quasi-compact open, cited from the morphisms and properties chapters
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the ideal whose Rees algebra presents the first blowing up and makes the relevant complements quasi-compact.

standard_prerequisites.name: The blowing up along a finite type ideal is an isomorphism away from the centre of the ideal, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the preimage of the complement of the first centre and keeps the complement of the union of the two images quasi-compact.

standard_prerequisites.name: The description of a closed subscheme of the blowing up as the blowing up of the base in a finite type submodule of a power of the defining ideal, supported outside a prescribed quasi-compact open, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the step that replaces the second centre, which a priori lives on the blowing up, by a single ideal on the base.

standard_prerequisites.name: The blowing up in a product of ideals equals the blowing up in the pulled back ideal, and blowing up in an invertible ideal, equivalently in an effective Cartier divisor, does not change the scheme, both cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the claim to the identification of two ideal sheaves on the second blowing up.

standard_prerequisites.name: The local description of an affine blowing up and of its blowup algebra, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the ideal equality into the elementary computation with a quotient of the form m over a to the d.

core_obligations: Translate the hypotheses into ideals: since the first centre is of finite presentation it is cut out by a finite type quasi-coherent ideal, and the blowing up is the projective spectrum of the Rees algebra of that ideal (proof lines 8675-8679).

Make the outer complement quasi-compact: the complement of the first centre is quasi-compact, the blowing up is an isomorphism over it, so the complement of the second centre inside that preimage is quasi-compact as well, and hence the complement of the union of the two images is quasi-compact open in the base (proof lines 8680-8687).

Replace the second centre by an ideal on the base: apply the cited description to find a positive integer d and a finite type submodule of the d-th power of the first ideal such that the second centre is the blowing up of the Rees algebra modulo that submodule and such that the quotient of the d-th power by the submodule is supported outside the quasi-compact open just found (proof lines 8687-8692).

Identify the union as a vanishing locus: reading the submodule as a finite type ideal inside the d-th power, its vanishing locus contains the first centre and, over the complement of that centre, cuts out exactly the second centre; hence the vanishing loci of the submodule and of its product with the first ideal both have underlying set the union of the two centres, and the product is again of finite type (proof lines 8694-8708).

Reduce to an equality of ideals on the second blowing up: by the cited product rule the blowing up of the base in that product is the blowing up of the first blowing up in the pullback of the submodule, so it suffices to show that this pullback equals the product of a power of the ideal of the exceptional divisor with the ideal of the second centre (proof lines 8710-8722).

Verify the equality locally: in the affine local model, the submodule corresponds to a submodule of the d-th power of the ideal mapping isomorphically to its image ideal, the second centre is locally cut out by the quotients of elements of that submodule by the d-th power of the chosen generator, and substituting the corresponding element of the image ideal makes the displayed equality immediate (proof lines 8724-8740).
proof_roadmap: Rewrite both centres through ideals: the first by a finite type ideal, the second by a finite type submodule of a power of it, chosen so that everything happens outside a quasi-compact open (proof lines 8675-8692).

Show that the product of the two ideals cuts out the union of the centres, then identify the two blowing ups up to an invertible twist of the centre, checking the ideal equality in the affine local model (proof lines 8694-8740).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that if one blows up a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme in a centre of finite presentation and then blows up the result in a further centre of finite presentation, the composite is again a blowing up of the original scheme, in a centre whose underlying closed subset is the union of the first centre with the image of the second (statement lines 8656-8673). The counted proof has two substantive layers: it replaces the second centre, which lives on the blowing up, by a finite type submodule of one power of the first ideal on the base, chosen so that the relevant quotients are supported outside a quasi-compact open, and it then identifies the two candidate blowing ups by comparing ideal sheaves on the second blowing up in the affine local model, where the computation reduces to writing an element as the d-th power of the chosen generator times the corresponding quotient (proof lines 8675-8740). It is H2: the reduction and the local computation are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the standard Rees algebra and blowing up statements.
